Strategy

Where we are (October 2026). DigiStayBook is built and running on its test address, but hasn’t launched. The Facebook Page (Digi Staybook) was created on 15 October with the logo, cover, bio and website link. There are no followers or customers yet.

The job of this period is an audience, not revenue. Before launch we want short-term rental hosts following the Page, and their own words about the questions guests ask and what they’d want from a digital guestbook. Those answers shape the launch messaging.

What we track until launch

MeasureWhere it’s readTarget
Page followersBusiness Suite → InsightsSet after week 1, once there’s a baseline
Comments from hostsThe posts that ask a question (Sat, Tue, Wed, Thu)Read and noted weekly
Reach per postBusiness Suite → ContentCompare post types week to week

No numbers are guessed in advance. The first week sets the baseline.

Constraints

  • Prelaunch: no prices, launch dates or sign-up links. The call to action is “follow the Page”.
  • Real product screens and the real logo only. No AI-generated people, scenes or photos in post images.
  • Seabreeze Cottage is a made-up demo property, and every post that shows it says so. No invented testimonials, customers or feedback.
  • Claude drafts; you approve. Posts sit in Business Suite as drafts until you publish or schedule them.

Who we talk to

  • Short-term rental hosts with one or a few properties, listing on Airbnb, Stayz or Booking.com, who answer the same guest questions every changeover.
  • Hosts who already leave a paper guestbook or a house manual, and would like guests to actually use it.

What we say

One QR code on the counter opens your house guidance, your local favourites and a wall of guest memories. No app and no account for guests.

  • Always: no app to download and no guest sign-up; the host stays in control (safety checks, approval, hide or remove posts); label the demo as a demo.
  • Never: promise a launch date or price before it’s set; suggest it gets hosts better reviews; present demo messages as real guests.

Channels

ChannelRoleRhythm
Facebook Page (Digi Staybook)Build a following of hosts before launchOne feed post a day in week 1, then review
Host Facebook groupsWhere hosts already talk (later, with each group’s rules)Not started
InstagramNot connected yetNot started

How the work runs

  1. Drafting: Claude writes each post, builds its image and saves it as a draft in Meta Business Suite, then sets its status here.
  2. Review: you review on this page (status and “Comment for Claude” on each card → Copy my review → paste to Claude).
  3. Publishing: you publish or schedule the draft on its day, or ask Claude to schedule it after your approval.

Needs you

Things only you can do
  • Delete the stray draft that starts “#ShortTermRental #HolidayRental…” in Business Suite, if you don’t need it (it may not show under the default date filter).
  • Fix where the website link goes: digistaybook.com shows a GoDaddy page, not the app, and the Page links there.
  • The cover image’s phone screen reads “DigiSook”. Replace the cover when you have a corrected version.
  • Close the leftover Business Suite tab in Chrome (an unfinished post from 15 Oct) and choose discard.

How to review a post
  • This week’s posts are all scheduled or posted. To change one, edit it under Scheduled in Business Suite before its time.
  • Facebook drafts don’t keep alt text. It’s in each post’s details; add it when you publish.
  • Captions that show the demo say it’s a made-up property. Keep that line if you edit them.
  • All times are Sydney time.

One row per post. Set the status as you review (your changes turn yellow and are saved in this browser), add comments in the post’s details, then press Copy my review and paste it to Claude, who makes it official. View ↓ jumps to the image and text.
